claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 4 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 4 years old and lives with you in the UK.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other basic needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I take care of Alex every day - I provide all his meals, buy his clothes, and look after all his basic needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. Now I need to ask about your residency status:

**Do you currently live in the UK? And if so, do you have the right to reside in the UK (for example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester. And yes, I have the right to reside here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

One final question:

**Is Alex in any of the following situations: in local authority care, in hospital for an extended period, or living with someone else (even temporarily)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex was in local authority care for a short period recently - just a couple of months. But he's back living with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that. I need to understand this situation a bit better:

**How long ago did Alex return to live with you? And since he's been back, has he been living with you continuously?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been back with me continuously since he returned. The time he was in care was just those couple of months I mentioned - it was about 4 weeks actually when I think about it more precisely.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying - so Alex was in care for about 4 weeks, and he's now back living with you continuously.

One more question about this:

**While Alex was in care during those 4 weeks, did he spend any regular time at home with you? For example, was he coming home for at least 24 hours per week, or spending at least 2 nights in a row each week with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, during those 4 weeks when he was in care, he was there full-time. He wasn't coming home to stay with me during that period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 4 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care and provide for his needs
- You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex was in local authority care for 4 weeks, but is now back living with you full-time

The key point here is that Alex was in care for 4 weeks, which is less than the 8-week threshold mentioned in the rules. According to the guidance, Child Benefit payments are affected if a child goes into care for **more than 8 weeks**. Since Alex was only in care for 4 weeks and is now back living with you, this should not affect your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- He lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for his care and provide for his needs
- You have the right to reside in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

The 4-week period when Alex was in care doesn't affect your eligibility since it was less than 8 weeks, and he's now back living with you full-time.

You can go ahead and apply for Child Benefit if you haven't already done so. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
